concepts.def: Healthy eating vocab: la fruta (fruit), las verduras (vegetables), el pescado (fish); la comida basura means junk food.
Sport: jugar al fútbol (play football) but hacer natación (do swimming) — jugar for games, hacer for activities.
Daily routine reflexives: me levanto (I get up), me ducho (I shower), me acuesto (I go to bed).
Saying what hurts: me duele la cabeza (my head hurts), me duelen las piernas (my legs hurt) — the verb agrees with the body part.
'Hay que' + infinitive means 'you have to / one must': Hay que beber mucha agua (You must drink lots of water).
'Desde hace' + time says how long: Juego al tenis desde hace dos años (I have been playing tennis for two years).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
